messages:
Jordan H: taking over APAC primary for tonight. quick summary: INC-2026-98 is still active in ap-southeast-1, errors on the embeddings pipeline (model-cache / kv-store path). paging started ~20:10 UTC, current status: degraded but customers only seeing intermittent 5xxs. handing off with actions-in-progress and a short plan.

Sam C: +1. I flipped the circuit-breaker for the model-cache service to 'soft' at 20:35 UTC to reduce fanout to downstream p99-slow nodes. command used: `curl -X POST $ADMIN/api/v1/cb/model-cache -d '{"state":"soft"}'` (logged in ops vault). This has cut the retry storm but error_rate still ~3.8%.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-98 created by pagerduty at 2026-02-14T20:12:03Z. Tags: embeddings, ap-southeast-1, customer-impact:partial. Priority: P2.

Nisha R: metrics snapshot at 20:40 UTC: embeddings-serve p50=220ms (baseline 110ms), p95=3.7s (baseline 1.2s), error_rate=3.8% (baseline 0.2%). Traffic skew: top customer calls from APAC increased due to customer batch jobs. KV-cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 74% on retry-heavy keys.

Jordan H: noted. Is this correlated with the nightly cache warm job?

Sam C: yes — we saw overlap with the cache-warm cron at 20:08 UTC. The cron triggered a full prefix scan which amplified writes to kv-store. I suppressed the cron (`kubectl patch cronjob cache-warm -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`) at 20:22 UTC. But node-level pressure persisted because of retries.

Alex P: trying a controlled rollback: routing 15% of embeddings traffic to quantized-2 (smaller) model to relieve memory pressure on large-hosts. Applied weighted route via routing service: `POST /routes/embeddings/weight { "quantized-2": 0.15 }`. Initial results: requests routed fine, lower mem usage on a subset of hosts.

Sam C: also kicked a targeted rolling restart of 3 kv-store pods (pods a,b,c) to clear stuck file descriptors — `kubectl rollout restart statefulset/kv-store -n infra --selector=kv-group=hot --max-unavailable=1`. Restarts finished by 20:50 UTC. Some short 502 spikes during pod cycling.

Nisha R: after restarts + routing changes: p95 trending down to 2.1s, error_rate down to 1.6% at 20:58 UTC. Still above baseline, but heading in right direction.

Jordan H: customer impact: a small subset of enterprise customers experienced 20-40% failed embeddings between 20:10-20:45 UTC. CS alerted major customers and provided workaround (retry with backoff). No data loss reported. Logging shows most failures were timeouts from downstream kv-store.

Alex P: FYI — I've opened a ticket with storage team to investigate compaction/backpressure on the shards involved (ST-721). Mentioned hot keys and cron overlap.

Sam C: current mitigations in place: circuit-breaker=soft, cache-warm cron suspended, 15% routing to quantized-2, 3 pod restarts, rate limiter increased for embed service to 150rps -> `scale config` change, and temporary request-level backoff enforced at gateway.

sre-bot: Runbook automation: step 4 (drain problematic hosts) marked IN_PROGRESS by Sam C at 20:46 UTC. Step 6 (notify account owners) marked COMPLETE.

Jordan H: handoff checklist for incoming primary/secondary:
- Primary (me): keep monitoring p95 and error_rate for embeddings-service and kv-store metrics.
- Secondary (Sam): owns rolling restarts / scaling actions, eligible to escalate to infra lead (Alex) if shard compaction suspected.
- Coverage gap: APAC midnight window (00:00-02:00 local) — no SRE on-site; I'll be available but would like someone to be ready to hand back by 02:30 UTC.

Jordan H: runbook pointers: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-kv-throttling (use the 'soft cb' pattern), and emergency fallback routing: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/fallback-routing. Use the 'notify-customers' template under playbooks.

Nisha R: monitoring to watch (dashboards): `infra/kv-store/latency`, `models/embeddings/p95`, `routing/weighting-breakdown`, `alerts/error-rate-embeddings`. Alerts: Sev2 if error_rate > 3% sustained 5m, Sev1 if >6% or data-loss flags.

Sam C: immediate next actions I will take after handoff: 1) confirm there are no more warm-cron triggers scheduled, 2) watch the throttle logs (`/var/logs/throttle.log`) for retry patterns, 3) keep the rolling restart plan ready if error_rate climbs back.

Jordan H: escalation contacts: infra lead @Alex P, product oncall @maria-p (if customer SLA breach), and exec notify if >30min widespread customer impact.

Alex P: follow-up items for post-incident: 1) change cron to staged-warm that pads over low traffic windows, 2) add shard-level circuit-breakers, 3) capacity plan for APAC rebalancing. I'll open RFCs after incident closure.

Nisha R: tagging expected recovery target: p95 <1.5s and error_rate <0.5% by 02:00 UTC. If not met, escalate for dedicated capacity in region.

Jordan H: handing over primary duty now. I'll stay on for 45m of overlap. If anything spikes, @Sam C please ping me on pager and post brief note in this thread. Leaving the current mitigations documented above.

Sam C: ack. I'll be on watch. Leaving a short run command snippet for incoming oncall:

```bash
# quick healthchecks
curl -sS $METRICS/api/embeddings/p95 | jq .value
kubectl get pods -l app=kv-store -n infra -o wide
curl -sS $ADMIN/api/v1/cb/model-cache | jq .state
```

Jordan H: thanks all. Signing off primary handoff at 21:00 UTC — will be reachable for 45m.

sre-bot: Thread archived: no further automated updates.
